title: Simultaneous determination of binary diffusion coefficients of hydrogen and methane in water and water-saturated porous media using a pressure decay method: experiments and modeling
content: Accurate measurement of gas diffusion coefficients in liquid-saturated porous media is essential for evaluating the performance and containment of underground gas storage systems, particularly for emerging underground hydrogen storage applications. However, experimental techniques that can directly determine these coefficients are scarce, and available data remain limited. This study introduces a novel model that simultaneously determines diffusion coefficients in bulk liquids and liquid-saturated porous media from a single pressure-decay experiment. By explicitly separating the pressure responses of the bulk liquid and porous-medium regions, the model estimates the bulk-liquid diffusion coefficient Db and the porous-medium parameter β, from which it estimates the effective diffusion coefficient Deff. We applied the approach to hydrogen–water and methane–water systems at 313.15–353.15 K and 5.17 MPa in a water-saturated Ottawa sand pack. The measured bulk-liquid diffusion coefficients are consistent with published data. The reported effective diffusion coefficients in porous media provide a new experimental dataset that helps address a significant gap in the literature. Both gases showed increasing diffusion coefficients with temperature, with methane showing a stronger relative temperature dependence Alt-text is not available for this image. than hydrogen, and thus a higher activation energy. The effective-to-bulk diffusivity ratio was about 0.23 for both hydrogen and methane, and the estimated apparent tortuosity was consistent with the Bruggeman correlation. The proposed method provides a simple, robust, and experimentally efficient approach to simultaneously characterize molecular diffusion in bulk liquids and liquid-saturated porous media, offering a valuable tool for evaluating gas containment and transport in underground methane and hydrogen storage reservoirs.
